Qatada used to say about this: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And he is blameworthy, meaning blameworthy in God’s blessings. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, And He is blameworthy, he said: He is blameworthy regarding the servants of God. He mentioned that this is in the reading of Abdullah: So We seized him and his soldiers and threw him away.
51:41: God Almighty says, And in Aad also, and what We did to them is a sign and a lesson for them, “when We sent upon them the barren wind. He means by the barren wind: the one that does not pollinate the trees. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The barren wind is the strong wind that does not fertilize anything. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, The barren wind, he said: It does not pollinate the trees nor stir up the clouds. Muhammad bin Amr told us: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, about this barren wind. He said: It has no mercy or vegetation, and it does not pollinate any plants. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Sulayman Abu Dawud told us: Shu’bah told us on the authority of Shas: I heard Al-Dahhak say about His statement, The barren wind, that it does not fertilize. Yaqub told me: Hisham told us: An old man from Khorasan, from the Azd tribe, whose nickname was Abu Sasan, told us: I asked Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim about his saying, The barren wind. He said: The wind that has no blessing and does not pollinate the trees. Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Hilali told us: Abu Ali Al-Hanafi told us: Ibn Abi Tha’lab told us, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, that he used to say: The barren wind is the south wind. Ahmad bin Al-Faraj told us: Ibn Abi Fadik told us: Ibn Abi Tha’lab told us on the authority of his maternal uncle Al-Harith bin Abd Al-Rahman, who said: Al-Aqeem means the south. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And to ‘Aad, when We sent upon them the barren wind. Indeed, some winds are barren and punishing when they are sent, for they do not fertilize anything. And some winds are mercy, by which God, Blessed and Exalted be He, stirs up the clouds and sends down rain. And it was mentioned to us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say, I was aided by the north wind, and ‘Aad was destroyed by the west wind. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, the barren wind, he said: The wind that does not produce vegetation. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, the barren wind: that which does not fertilize anything. Ibn Hamid told me: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan, who said: The barren wind is the one that does not produce anything. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And in the tribe of ‘Aad, when We sent upon them the barren wind, he said: God, the Blessed and Exalted, sends the wind as a good tiding before His mercy, and He revives with it the root and the tree, and these do not fertilize nor do they revive. They are barren, and there is nothing good in them. They are merely a torment that does not fertilize anything, and these do fertilize. And he recited, And We sent the fertilizing winds Al-Hijr 22.
51:42: And his saying, It leaves nothing it comes upon except that it makes it like dust. And dust in the speech of the Arabs is: what dries up from the plants of the earth and is trampled. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention who said that, even though their expressions differed. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, It does not leave anything it comes upon except that it makes it like chaff, meaning like something that has perished. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, like ashes, like a perishing thing. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: Kalameem means the ashes of trees. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Except that I will make it like the ashes of a tree, he said: Like the ashes of a tree.
51:43: God Almighty says: And in Thamud there is also for them a lesson and admonition, when their Lord said to them: They were arrogant towards the command of their Lord and were haughty in their disobedience to God. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, They acted arrogantly, he said: They were haughty. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, So they rebelled against the command of their Lord, he said: The rebellious one is the one who abandons the command of God. And His saying, So the thunderbolt seized them, God Almighty says, So the thunderbolt of punishment seized them suddenly. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention who said that. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, So the thunderbolt seized them while they were looking on, while they were waiting. That is because Thamud had promised the punishment three days before it would descend upon them and had made signs for its descent upon them in those three days. So the signs that were made for them indicating its descent appeared in those days, so on the fourth day they became certain that the punishment was about to descend upon them and were awaiting its arrival. The reciters of the regions, except for Al-Kisa’i, read So the thunderbolt seized them with an alif. It was narrated on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that he read that, So the thunderbolt seized them without an alif. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi, that Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, recited: The thunderbolt took them. Al-Kisa’i recited it in the same way, and with the alif we recite the thunderbolt, because the authoritative reciters agreed on it.
51:44: God Almighty said: But they rebelled against the command of their Lord, so the thunderbolt seized them while they were looking on.
51:45: God Almighty says: They were not able to defend themselves against the punishment of God that befell them, nor were they able to withstand it. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And they were not able to stand, he said: The people were not able to stand up because of the punishment of God, the Blessed and Exalted. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: So they were not able to stand. He said: To stand. Some Arab scholars used to say: The meaning of his saying, So they were not able to stand is So they did not stand up. He said: If it had been So they were not able to stand up, it would have been correct, and the alif would have been removed from it, like his saying, He caused you to grow from the earth a plant Noah 17. His saying, And they were not victorious, means: They were not able to benefit from those who inflicted the punishment that befell them. Qatada used to say in his interpretation of that: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And they were not victorious. He said: They did not have the strength to protect themselves from God Almighty.
51:46: And his saying, And the people of Noah before, indeed, they were a people of transgressors. The reciters differed in reading his saying, And the people of Noah, in the accusative case. There are several reasons for this accusative case: One of them is that the people is in apposition to the ha and the mim in his saying, So the thunderbolt seized them, since every destructive punishment is called a thunderbolt by the Arabs. So the meaning of the statement then is: So the thunderbolt seized them and seized the people of Noah before. The second is that it is in the accusative case in the sense of the statement, since in what has passed of the report of the nations before it was an indication of what was intended from the statement and its meaning is: We destroyed these nations and destroyed the people of Noah before. The third is that an accusative verb is implied for it, so the meaning of the statement is: And mention to them the people of Noah, as he said, And Abraham, when he said to his people Al-Ankabut 16 and the like, meaning inform them and mention to them. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read this and the people of Noah in the accusative case with the meaning: And in the people of Noah, in apposition to the people, to Moses in his saying, And in Moses, when We sent him to Pharaoh. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings in the readings of the regions, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. The interpretation of this in the reading of the one who reads in the khufd is: “And in the people of Noah, for them also is a lesson, when We destroyed them before Thamud when they denied Our Messenger Noah. “Indeed, they were a wicked people.” He says: They were disobeying God’s command and going against His obedience.
51:47: God Almighty says: And the sky We raised as a ceiling with strength. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention who said that. Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And the heaven We constructed with power, meaning: with strength. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, with hands, he said: with strength. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And the heaven We constructed with power: meaning with strength. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us on the authority of Mansur that he said regarding this verse, And the heaven We constructed with power, he said: with strength. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And the heaven We constructed with power, he said: with strength. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan: And the heaven We constructed with power. He said: Strongly. And His statement: And indeed, We are indeed All-Encompassing means: He has the capacity to create it and to create whatever We will to create and has the power to do it. And from this is His statement: Upon the one with plenty is his capacity and upon the one with miserliness is his capacity Al-Baqarah 236. What is meant by this is the strong one. Ibn Zayd said about this: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And indeed, We are expanding it, that He, the Most High, the Majestic, has expanded it.
51:48: And His statement, And the earth We have spread out, God Almighty says: And the earth We have made a bed for creation. And excellent are the spreaders, meaning: We are excellent spreaders for them.
51:49: God Almighty says: And We created of everything We created in pairs. And We left out the first creation, as the evidence of the speech was sufficient for it. There is a difference of opinion about the meaning of We created in pairs. Some of them said: It means that of everything We created two different types, such as misery and happiness, guidance and misguidance, and so on. Mention who said that. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Ibn Jurayj told us: Mujahid said regarding His statement, And of everything We created pairs, he said: Disbelief and faith, misery and happiness, guidance and misguidance, night and day, heaven and earth, mankind and jinn. Ibn Bashar told us: Ibrahim bin Abi Al-Wazir told us: Marwan bin Muawiyah Al-Fazari told us: Aouf told us on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement, And of everything We created pairs, he said: The sun and the moon. Others said: What he meant by the pair is the male and female. Mention who said that. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement, And of everything We created pairs, he said: Male and female, that is the pair. And he recited, And We made his wife good for him Al-Anbiya’ 90, he said: His wife. The first of the two opinions on this is the opinion of Mujahid, which is that God, the Blessed and Exalted, created for everything He created a second to it, different in meaning, so each one of them is a pair for the other. That is why it was said: We created pairs. The Most High, with His praise, only drew attention to His ability to create whatever He wills to create from a thing, and that He is not like the things whose nature is to do one type without its opposite, since everything whose description is the action of one type without what is other than it, like fire whose nature is to heat and is not suitable for cooling, and like snow whose nature is to cool and is not suitable for heating. It is not permissible to describe it with perfection, but rather the perfection of praise belongs to the One who is able to do whatever He wills to do from the different and similar things. And His saying, Perhaps you will remember, means: So that you may remember and reflect on this, and learn, O polytheists, that your Lord, who requires you to worship Him, is the One who has the power to create a thing and its opposite, and to invent pairs of everything, not something that He is not capable of doing.
51:50: God Almighty says: So flee, O people, from God’s punishment to His mercy by believing in Him, following His commands, and working in obedience to Him. Indeed, I am to you a warner from Him. He says: I am to you a warner from God, warning you of His punishment and frightening you of His torment that He brought upon these nations whose stories He has related to you, and which He will make them taste in the Hereafter. His saying: Mubeen means he makes his warning clear to you.
51:51: And His statement, And do not make with God another god, God Almighty says: And do not make, O people, with your god who created you another god other than Him, for there is no god worthy of worship other than Him. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner, He says: Indeed, I am to you, O people, a clear warner of His punishment for your worshipping a god other than Him. He has made the warning clear to you.
51:52: God Almighty says: Just as the Quraysh denied their prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: He is a poet, a magician, or a madman, so did the nations that denied their messengers, upon whom God brought His vengeance, such as the people of Noah, Aad, Thamud, and Pharaoh and his people. These people whom we mentioned before them, meaning before the Quraysh, the people of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not come to anyone except that they said: He is a magician or a madman, just as the Quraysh said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
51:53: And His statement, “They enjoin it upon one another. Rather, they are a transgressing people.” God Almighty says: Did these deniers from Quraysh enjoin Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, upon what he brought them of the truth, their forefathers and their fathers who had passed before them, by belying Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they accepted that from them? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention who said that. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: “They enjoin it upon one another. Rather, they are a transgressing people.” He said: The first of them enjoined the last of them to deny it. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, They enjoined it upon one another, meaning that the first had enjoined the second to deny it. And His statement, Rather, they are a transgressing people, God Almighty says: These polytheists did not command their last ones to do that, but they are a transgressing people who transgress against the command of their Lord, who do not obey His command nor desist from what He forbade them from.
51:54: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So turn away, O Muhammad, from these polytheists from Quraysh. He says: So turn away from them until God’s command comes to you concerning them. It is said: So-and-so turned away from so-and-so: if he turned away from him and abandoned him, as Husayn ibn Damdam said: As for the Banu Abs, their hybrid turned away from his horsemen and escaped with one eye. In this context, the one-eyed person is the one who is blind and whose need is not met or who does not get what he wants. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: Turn away from them. He said: Turn away from them. And His saying, So you are not to be blamed, means that He, the Most High, says, “So you, O Muhammad, are not to be blamed. Your Lord does not blame you for any negligence on your part in warning, for you have warned and conveyed that with which you were sent.” And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Then turn away from them, for you are not to be blamed, he said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, Then turn away from them, for you are not to be blamed, He said: You have conveyed that with which We sent you, so you are not to be blamed. He said: How can he blame him when he has conveyed what I have sent him with? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Then turn away from them, for you are not to be blamed. It was mentioned to us that when this verse was revealed, the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were distressed and they saw that the revelation had been cut off and that the punishment had come. So God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed after that, And remind, for the reminder benefits the believers. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me: Ibn Ali narrated to us: Ayoub narrated to us, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Ali came out wearing a cloak and a shawl, and when the verse, Then turn away from them, for you are not to be blamed, was revealed, we were saddened by that and we said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that he turn away from us until the verse, And remind, for the reminder benefits the believers, was revealed.
51:55: And his saying, And remind, for the reminder benefits the believers, means: Preach, O Muhammad, to whomever you are sent, for preaching benefits the people of faith in God. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid: And remind, for the reminder benefits the believers. He said: Admonish them.
51:56: The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of His statement, And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. Some of them said: The meaning of this is: I did not create the happy ones among the jinn and mankind except to worship Me, and the wretched ones among them to disobey Me. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam: And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. He said: What they were created with of misery and happiness. Ibn Bashar told us: Muammil told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, in a similar manner. Abdul-A’la bin Wasil told me: Ubaidullah bin Musa told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, something similar. Humaid bin Al-Rabi’ Al-Kharraz told us: Ibn Yaman told us: Ibn Jurayj told us on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam regarding his statement, And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me, he said: He created them for misery and happiness. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan: And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. He said: He who was created for the sake of distance. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: I did not create the jinn and mankind except to submit to Me in worship. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me, except to acknowledge worship willingly or unwillingly. The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the one we mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas, which is: I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Us and to submit to Our command. If someone says: How could they have disbelieved when He created them to submit to His command? They submitted to His decree that He decreed upon them, because His decree is binding upon them and they are unable to avoid it if it befalls them. Rather, those who disbelieved in Him disobeyed Him by doing what He commanded them to do. As for submitting to His decree, then it is not impossible to avoid it.
51:57: And His statement: I do not want from them any provision means that God Almighty says: I do not want from those I created of the jinn and mankind any provision that they provide to My creation. And I do not want them to feed means: I do not want from them any sustenance that they should be sustained and any food that they should feed them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Muadh bin Hisham told us: My father told us, on the authority of Amr bin Malik, on the authority of Abu al-Juza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want them to feed themselves. He said: They feed themselves.
51:58: God Almighty says: Indeed, it is God who provides for His creation and takes care of their sustenance, the Possessor of strength, the Sturdy. The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement Al-Matin. The majority of reciters of the regions, except Yahya ibn Waththab and Al-A’mash, recited it as Dhu al-Quwwa al-Matin in the nominative case, meaning: Dhu al-Quwwa al-Matin. They made al-Matin an adjective for Dhu and directed it to describing God with it. Yahya and Al-A’mash recited it as Al-Matin in the genitive case, making it an adjective for strength. The one who recited it in the genitive case permitted the genitive case, making it an adjective for strength. Strength is feminine, and Al-Matin is masculine in its expression, because he removed strength from Qawwa strong rope and the twisted thing: the twisting. So it is as if he said according to this doctrine: Dhu al-Habl al-Qawwa strong rope. Al-Farra’ mentioned that some Arabs recited it: For every age I have worn a garment of Rita and the right hand bandaged So Al-Mu'asab made the right hand an adjective, although it is feminine in pronunciation, because the right hand is a type and a kind of clothing, so he went with it to that. The correct reading for this in our view is the Possessor of strength, the Mighty in the nominative case, as it is an attribute of God, may He be glorified, due to the consensus of the jurists on this, and if it were an attribute of strength, then the feminine form would have been more appropriate, even though there is a reason for the masculine form. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, the strong, the mighty, meaning: the powerful.
51:59: And His statement, For those who have wronged are sins like the sins of their companions, so let them not be impatient. God Almighty says: For those who associated partners with God from among the Quraysh and others are sins, which is the great bucket, which is also the register, if it is filled or almost filled. What is meant by sins in this place is: the portion and the share. From this is the saying of Alqamah bin Abdah: And in every nation you have been blessed with a blessing, so it is right for someone to commit sins because of your call. Any share and its origin is what I mentioned and from it the rajaz poet said: We have sins and you have sins. If you refuse, then we have the heart. The meaning of the words: Those who have wronged will have a share and portion of God’s punishment that will descend upon them, similar to the share of their companions who followed their path before them, from the punishment, so they should not hasten it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, For those who have wronged there are sins, meaning: a bucket. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, For those who have wronged will be sins similar to the sins of their companions. He said: He says that for those who have wronged will be a punishment similar to the punishment of their companions, so they should not be impatient. Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr: Sins like the sins of their companions. So they should not be hasty: a record of punishment. He said: Affan bin Muslim told us: Shihab bin Saree’ah told us on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement, sins like the sins of their companions, he said: A bucket like the bucket of their companions. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Sinubun means a record. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, For those who have wronged there are sins is a record of God’s punishment. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, For those who have wronged will be sins like the sins of their companions. He said: A punishment like the punishment of their companions. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, For those who have wronged are sins like the sins of their companions, he said, He means sins of punishment. He said, He says to them, a record of God’s punishment, and He did this to their companions before them, so for them is a punishment like the punishment of their companions, so they should not hasten. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Ibrahim: Sins like the sins of their companions. He said: A portion of the punishment.
51:60: God Almighty says: The flowing valley in Hell of pus and blood for those who disbelieved in God and denied His Oneness from the day on which they are promised the descent of God’s punishment when it descends upon them, what affliction and hardship they will encounter therein.
